## Code and output

```{r code, echo = TRUE}
d <- tibble(group = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 5), y = c(3, 4, 5, 4, 6, 7, 8, 6, 9, 8))
d |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(y), sd = sd(y))
```

## A figure

```{r pooling, fig.height = 3.9}
set.seed(27)
pp <- tibble(id = sprintf("S%02d", 1:14), n = sample(3:30, 14, replace = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(true = rnorm(14, 500, 40),
         raw = true + rnorm(14, 0, 120 / sqrt(n)),
         pooled = (raw * n + 500 * 8) / (n + 8),
         id = fct_reorder(id, raw))
ggplot(pp, aes(y = id)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 500, colour = muted, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = raw, xend = pooled, yend = id), colour = vine, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = raw, colour = "No pooling"), size = 3.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = pooled, colour = "Partial pooling"), size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`No pooling` = pandan, `Partial pooling` = kingfisher)) +
  labs(x = "Mean reaction time (ms)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

Simulated data. Speakers with few observations move furthest toward the grand mean.

## A table

| Model | Random effects | AIC |
|---|---|---|
| m0 | intercepts by subject | 4210.3 |
| m1 | intercepts and slopes by subject | 4187.9 |
| m2 | m1, plus intercepts by item | 4176.4 |

## Summary

::: {.takeaway}
- [Partial pooling]{.hl} pulls noisy group estimates toward the grand mean
- Groups with less data move further
:::

## References {.refs}

- Student (1908). The probable error of a mean. _Biometrika_, 6(1), 1–25.
